newsitem.title: UK: UK shares advance amid short squeeze.
newsitem.headline: UK shares advance amid short squeeze.

text.p: The UK's leading blue chip shares advanced at the open on Tuesday on what dealers described as a low-volume short squeeze.
At 0748 GMT, the benchmark FTSE 100 share index was up 41.2 points to 4,936.9, as advancers broadly beat decliners 84 to six.
They said the lack of bad news on the corporate front precipitated the unexpected rally.
"Everyone's results met expectations. Even NatWest's numbers weren't particularly poor," said one dealer.
BAA Plc shares jumped 14-1/2p, or 2.6 percent, to 575 after the UK airport management group said its first quarter profits rose to 136.0 million stg, as expected, from 130.0 million stg a year ago.
However, shares in National Westminster Bank fell 11-1/2p to 858-1/2p after it reported first half pre-tax profits from continuing operations rose to 775 million stg from 662 million a year ago.
Later this morning, British Petroleum Plc will post its second quarter results. Profits in the latest quarter were expected near 661.0 million stg, up from 587.0 million stg a year ago.
Pharmaceutical shares were buoyant after Glaxo Wellcome Plc and SmithKline Beecham Plc ADRs rose overnight.
Rising crude oil prices lifted UK oil shares as well. British Petroleum shares led the rise, gaining 11-1/2p to 833-1/2p.
Yet trading volume is expected to remain light ahead of the Bank of England's two-day monetary policy meeting, starting on Thursday, they said.
"I'm afraid that the uncertainty about interest rates will keep volumes low and markets volatile," another dealer said.
Dealers said the FTSE futures market, responsible for much of Monday's volatility, could continue to jar thin markets today.
"Buyers are still around, but they're not aggressive," another dealer said. "But if anyone sees blood in the water, they'll start selling."
A slew of economic data could influence trading today, though the impact is likely to be limited ahead of the Bank of England's monetary meeting, dealers said.
At 0830 GMT, the UK purchasing managers survey, industrial production and manufacturing output are due for release. At 1000 GMT, the CBI regional trends survey will be published.
Gilts were slightly firmer ahead of the data.
